expunge

/ik-SPUNJ/ - rhymes with plunge · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Expunge means to obliterate or erase completely.

The treaty's final clause expunged the old debts from every ledger on both sides of the border.

Example

After the mix-up was traced to a scanner error, the clinic expunged the false allergy flag from the patient's chart and from every backup its vendor held.

Expunge is stronger than delete or remove because nothing survives it — no note, no asterisk, no copy in a drawer. The entry is not corrected or hidden; it is made never to have been.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

delete: Delete means to remove an entry from a file or document, but copies often survive on backups or in other drawers. Expunge goes all the way: the record is destroyed everywhere, officially and completely, as though it had never been made.

redact: Redact means to black out sensitive parts of a document so readers cannot see them, while the document itself survives, bars and all. Expunge is total: nothing is hidden behind a bar, because the entry itself ceases to exist anywhere.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

enshrine: fix something permanently in an honored place

inscribe: write or cut something in so that it lasts

Where it sits · how completely the record disappears

blot → erase → expunge

blot vs. expunge: Blot is far milder than expunge — ink smeared over the entry, which a patient eye can still read beneath the stain, while an expunged record leaves nothing behind to read at all.

erase vs. expunge: Erase is milder than expunge even when it is clean: an erased line can survive in copies and carbon sheets, while an expunged record is destroyed everywhere, as though never made.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ex-: out

Root — punge: to prick (Latin pungere)

Put it together: Ex- (out) + punge (to prick, from Latin pungere) = to prick out. Roman clerks struck a name from a roll by pricking a row of dots beneath it — the entry was 'pointed out' of existence. The prickly root survives in puncture and pinpoint. To expunge a record is to do with finality what those dots once did: put it beyond reading, everywhere.

Use the root in a new word: puncture: A roofing nail punctured the rear tire two blocks from home.

Word Building

Word Choice

formal / legal

Expunge belongs to records — court files, transcripts, rolls, databases — and promises total, official annihilation of an entry. Efface, taught in this unit, wears a mark off a physical surface; expurgate, also in this unit, cleans a text of its offensive parts but leaves the text standing. When a lawyer says a conviction was expunged, she means the law now treats it as never having existed.
